title: Salaried office employee, single, Bangkok
conversation:
Hi, I'm Nok. I'm 32, single, and I work as an admin officer at a logistics company in Bangkok. I'm starting my finances over on 1 January 2026, so let's use that as the starting date. Nothing from 2025 carries into this plan, and any tax on last year's income is already dealt with.

My salary is 60,000 baht a month before tax, and it goes up with inflation each year, so please let it grow at the inflation rate. Social security takes 750 baht a month, which comes to 9,000 baht a year. I pay life insurance of 12,000 baht a year and health insurance of 6,000 baht a year.

I spend about 32,000 baht a month on rent, food, transport and bills, and that goes up with inflation too. My social security, life insurance and health insurance are already inside those 32,000 baht, so don't add them again. I put 15,000 baht a month into a mutual fund, and that stays at 15,000 baht for the whole plan: it does not rise with inflation. Whatever is left over goes into my savings account.

Right now I have 350,000 baht in savings earning about 1% a year, and 900,000 baht in the mutual fund, which has averaged about 5% a year. Inflation I'm assuming at 2.5%.

I want to know two things. When can I stop working, meaning when could I live on my savings and fund without my salary? And what is my 2026 income tax? After that, I'd like to know what changes if my living costs drop to 27,000 baht a month.

whatIf.description: my living costs drop to 27,000 baht a month
